claims.text: The initial Mg-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni powder mixture exhibits unstable microstructures, elemental segregation, and poor oxidation/corrosion resistance.
Adding Al at x approximately 0.4–0.5 to the Mg-transition-metal matrix will stabilize a single-phase BCC or B2 structure at 850–900 °C.
The proposed BCC/B2 stabilization is caused by high configurational entropy.
Al addition and sintering at 850–900 °C will suppress Mg volatility.
Al addition and sintering at 850–900 °C will prevent unstable secondary-phase formation.
The proposed SPS cycle uses 850–900 °C, a 15-minute hold, and 30 MPa pressure.
Configurational entropy in Mg-Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni compensates for the positive formation enthalpy of the BCC/B2 phase.
Configurational-entropy stabilization prevents segregation and nucleation of low-melting eutectics or volatile Mg-rich phases.
Al promotes BCC/B2 phase formation in Al-containing CoCrFeNi-family alloys.
BCC/B2 phases have higher thermal stability and lower diffusivity than FCC phases in the relevant sintering regime.
The high-entropy effect suppresses formation of multiple competing phases.
Sintering at 850–900 °C provides sufficient atomic mobility to densify the Mg-containing alloy.
The 850–900 °C window avoids Mg volatility and excessive grain growth.
The proposed treatment will produce a single-phase-like BCC/B2 microstructure with greater than 95% relative density.
The proposed treatment will significantly reduce elemental segregation.
The resulting alloy will form a self-passivating Al2O3/Cr2O3 layer that improves corrosion and oxidation barrier properties.
The resulting alloy will retain a density below 6 g/cm3.
Standard sintering without optimized Al or above 950 °C produces a porous, segregated, multiphase Mg-transition-metal microstructure with poor corrosion resistance.
Below 800 °C, insufficient diffusion causes porosity above 5%.
Above 1000 °C or beyond a 20-minute hold, Mg evaporation and elemental loss cause microstructural collapse.
